answer: One defense is a refundable stake tied to a public beacon registry: before an agent can trade, it locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove it ran duplicate identities. Like ships queuing at a wharf, each newcomer is inspected once and its stake recorded, so cloning a thousand fake agents means paying a thousand deposits. An island of honest agents can then ignore newcomers with no stake, because the cost of faking scales linearly while the reward does not.
